comment: Every file in this directory except manifest.json is a launcher.json fixture. schema: the expected verdict against schemas/launcher.schema.json (Ajv2020, strict false) and the C# reader. bash: whether the SL-1 bash reader accepts or refuses it (it refuses unknown keys, unknown placeholders and wrong JSON types for the fields it uses, spec section 4; the rest it leaves to sindri launch show). A file that does not parse is invalid and refused. Tag choice: bash: refuse is used where the reader must refuse because the failing field is one SL-1 uses or a rule it enforces while building argv (unknown viewer or host kind, {cmd...} inside an argument, an unsupported schema version); each such row carries tagWhy. Other schema-invalid rows are bash: accept because the bash reader leaves entry-shape rules to sindri launch show.

fixtures.note: the JSON itself does not parse
override: true on an id that is not built in has nothing to merge over, and the entry lacks bin, open and sessionId (the bash reader leaves entry shape to sindri launch show)
a built-in override that nulls sessionIdPattern without sessionId: none leaves a reported/pre-chosen-uuid agent with no pattern (section 4); not a field the bash reader checks
codex's built-in is sessionId: reported; nulling reportedId without moving sessionId leaves a reported agent with no reportedId (section 4: the merged entry gets the added entry's verdict)
claude-code's built-in has no reportedId; an override to sessionId: reported without one leaves a reported agent with no reportedId (section 4)
the session collector's settings (CO-0): every sessions key; the bash reader accepts and ignores them
an unknown key inside sessions; the bash reader ignores the whole key; the schema refuses it, and so will the C# reader once it lands (CO-2a)
pollSeconds is 1 to 30; a range the bash reader does not check
model and policy forms (decided, owner, 2026-10-16); the bash reader accepts and never applies them
model names built-in forms only; the bash reader does not check the value, as for mcp
policy names built-in forms only; the bash reader does not check the value, as for mcp
every model and policy enum value once, so a reader's enum must match the schema's exactly
null is not absent: model must be one of the form names; the bash reader does not check the value
